clue.text: Pretty Welsh girl widely thought not to be all there

indicators.note: only part of the two words is present, so the answer sits inside them rather than being the whole

explanation.surface: A Welsh beauty is generally considered a bit dim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to be all there' reads as an insult but signals that only part of 'widely thought' is used: the run DELYTH spans the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh given name is traditionally glossed as meaning pretty, so a pretty Welsh girl fits it.

clue.text: "Will you marry me", say, that's forward also rude!

parts.note: in rugby a prop is one of the forwards

indicators.note: rude in the sense of rough or unpolished, so the letters of also are knocked into a cruder order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a marriage offer is both pushy and impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' reads as cheeky, which fits 'rude', but it is the rugby position. 'Rude' then reorders the letters of 'also'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to marry you is the classic example of an offer of marriage, so the question exemplifies it.

clue.text: Set switched on however causes most static

parts.note: still can mean however, nevertheless

indicators.note: switched round, so the letters of the word set change places

explanation.surface: A television set turned on generates the most electrical interference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set switched on' reads as a television being turned on; 'switched' is the anagram signal and 'on' places the result after the synonym of 'however'.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving, so the most static thing is the most motionless, the superlative of still.

clue.text: As well to tour red light area in Spain

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second, as a tourist circles a place

parts.note: as well means too
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a small indicator light, often red

explanation.surface: Also, take a trip round the red-light district in a Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To tour' wraps one piece round the other. 'Red light area' suggests a sleazy district, but the definition is just 'area in Spain'.
explanation.definitionFit: This historic city and province lies in central Spain, so it is an area there.

clue.text: An agreement old car's what gradually gets you over the hill

definitions.text: what gradually gets you over the hill

parts.note: a nod signals agreement
the Mini is a classic small British car; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a nod, an old car and what ageing does.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'in the year of the Lord'; the clue uses it in its humorous sense of advancing age.
explanation.definitionFit: As a humorous idiom the Latin dating phrase stands for old age, which slowly carries people past their prime.

clue.text: Transmission, finally, clear without that crackling?

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to clear of something is to rid it

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a broadcast can be cleaned of its crackly interference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives N, the last letter of 'Transmission', and 'without' (outside) puts RID round it. Crackling here is not radio noise but pork skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp roasted skin of pork, which is the outer layer of the meat.

clue.text: Bath for one that's cold and regularly filthy

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bath that is cold and usually dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'filthy': ITY. Bath is the English city, not a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath, in Somerset, is an English settlement with official status, an example of the urban category.

clue.text: Drink: all the same name and variety

parts.note: but in the sense of nevertheless
a term is a word or name for something
ilk means kind or variety

explanation.surface: A drink, but described as being the same name and type.
explanation.definitionFit: The sour liquid left after churning cream is drunk, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Wearing uniform: fit that can expand?

parts.note: to be in clothes is to be wearing them
flat in the sense of even and level
fit and able both mean capable

explanation.surface: Someone in uniform asks whether the fit allows room to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' suggests clothing but means even, FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be blown up with air is able to swell, so it is a thing capable of expanding.

clue.text: Criticism's outspoken for oil-producing plant

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: flak is criticism; with the 's it becomes flak's

explanation.surface: Someone says frank criticism is aimed at a crop grown for oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' looks like bluntness but signals a sound-alike: FLAK'S said aloud matches the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Linseed oil is pressed from the seeds of this crop, so it is a plant yielding oil.

clue.text: Fancy that fellow's after wife

indicators.note: the fellow comes after the wife in the answer

parts.note: him refers to a man already mentioned

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a man is pursuing a married woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that' reads as an exclamation, but 'Fancy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy in the sense of a sudden passing desire or caprice is a synonym.

clue.text: Fitting something inside shelter only after test

indicators.note: the test and only go within the shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: only comes after test in the answer

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars
just means only

explanation.surface: Someone fits something into a shelter, but only after passing a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' places the test and 'only' within the shelter. The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety check, so 'test' is a fair hint.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means the exactly right word, so it is something that fits perfectly.

clue.text: Groom in drama because a present returned unwrapped

indicators.note: the wrapping is taken off, removing the outermost letters
returned means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: for means because
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: In a play a gift is given back without its wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reverses FOR A GIFT to TFIGAROF, and 'unwrapped' removes the outer T and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera and Beaumarchais's play feature the barber whose wedding is the plot, so he is a stage bridegroom.

clue.text: Following hindrance, one false step performed recklessly?

indicators.note: the one and false step follow the hindrance

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'
I is the Roman numeral one
a trip is a stumble

explanation.surface: After an obstacle, someone stumbles while acting rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go all out without restraint, so it describes acting in an unrestrained, rash way.

clue.text: Opening bottles transformed third anniversary

indicators.note: bottles in the sense of contains, holding one piece inside another

parts.note: a bay is an opening, as in a window bay or loading bay

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of third are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Opening bottles of wine for a third wedding anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening bottles' looks like uncorking wine; 'transformed' reorders the clue word third and 'bottles' means holds it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual return of the day you were born is the most familiar kind of anniversary.

clue.text: Requests woman's placed with her organisation?

indicators.note: the woman's piece is put next to the organisation

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation
she's, a woman is

explanation.surface: A woman is put alongside her club and makes demands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute (WI) is a British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishes in the sense of expressed desires are things asked for, so they are requests.

clue.text: What should observe planning regulation that's now relaxed?

definitions.meaning: a house addition, which needs planning permission
read as ..., stress that is in the past

explanation.surface: Someone notes a building rule has been loosened.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: someone relaxed has tension that is now former, 'ex'.
explanation.definitionFit: A home addition needs planning permission in Britain, and the playful split gives former stress.

clue.text: Canary, rather unhappy, in back of aviary, see

indicators.note: back of takes the final letter of the word
the sad piece goes inside the other letters

parts.note: Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is a cathedral city and bishop's see
low means sad

explanation.surface: A canary, rather glum, sits at the back of its aviary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back of' gives the final letter of 'aviary'; 'in' puts the sad word inside. A see is a bishop's district, here the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary yellow is a colour, so somewhat canary-coloured means tinged with that colour.

clue.text: Aspect of Jumbo that's not good

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: jumbo means enormous

explanation.surface: Some aspect of an elephant named Jumbo isn't nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo suggests the elephant, but it is an adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a shade or complexion, which is a sense of aspect as appearance.

clue.text: Little boys not dressed in green strike one

parts.note: a putt is a stroke played on a golf green
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Naked little boys hit one in the green.
explanation.walkthrough: Putti are the naked cherubs of Renaissance art.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherub figures in art are small naked boys, so little boys without clothes fits.

clue.text: Footballer, slim, was willing

parts.note: an outside chance is a slim one
left in a will, bequeathed

explanation.surface: A thin footballer was prepared to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was willing' means bequeathed by will, LEFT. An outside left was an old-fashioned left winger.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional forward position on the left wing, so the player is a footballer.

clue.text: One's content could be crude, loud: I'm right to be upset

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disarranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone's rude and loud, and insists they are right to be angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be upset' rearranges LOUD, IM and R. 'Crude' is oil, not rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is stored and shipped in large metal barrels, so such a container's contents may be crude.

clue.text: Promotion academic — or peripheral

parts.note: an ad promotes a product
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A promotion for an academic, or something marginal.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra attachment is supplementary, like a computer peripheral that is plugged on.

clue.text: Bypass orator messing with ad-lib

indicators.note: messing with means jumbling the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A speaker improvises about a new bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messing with' rearranges ORATOR and ADLIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring road around a town lets traffic avoid the centre, a kind of bypass.

clue.text: Unwieldy vessel is one blown, almost to the end

indicators.note: it runs almost to its end, losing the final letter

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument that is blown

explanation.surface: A clumsy boat is blown nearly to its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost to the end' drops the final A of TUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is slang for a slow, clumsy boat, so it is an awkward vessel.

clue.text: Origin and description of the Magi overshadowed by Liberal, however

indicators.note: in a down clue, the Liberal sits on top of the rest

parts.note: the Magi came from the East
they are called the Wise Men

explanation.surface: A Liberal casts a shadow over the Nativity's wise men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overshadowed by' puts L above EAST + WISE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at least or anyway, a sense of however as a qualifier.

clue.text: Meat resembling tripe's first seen in pan

parts.note: lamb is a meat
as means like, resembling

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Lamb, like tripe, is cooked in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like cookware but is a verb meaning to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a show is to criticise it severely, which is to berate harshly.

clue.text: Doctor of note trained at first in America twice

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the letter sits within the doubled country
twice means the abbreviation is used two times

parts.note: US is America

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of trained

explanation.surface: A doctor of music trained first in America, twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' gives T from 'trained'; 'in' puts it within USUS, made by 'twice'. Marlowe's Doctor Faustus is the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlowe's tragedy is titled with this scholar's name and the honorific Doctor.

clue.text: Starts off having an interesting time in the country

indicators.note: starts of the words, their opening letters

explanation.surface: Someone begins an exciting stay abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' takes the first letters of 'having an interesting time in'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Caribbean nation sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic is a country.

clue.text: Graduate wouldn't stand for this language

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
lay, past tense of lie, as opposed to standing

explanation.surface: A graduate won't put up with this language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wouldn't stand for' reads as 'tolerate', but 'wouldn't stand' means lay (lay down).
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of Malaysia and neighbouring lands is a language.

clue.text: Draw up set of Biblical books, ending in Matthew

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

indicators.note: ending in takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Drawing up a group of Bible books finishing with Matthew.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a vehicle behind is to pull it, so the verbs are synonyms.
